questions.question_text: Which of the following errors is not disclosed by a Trial Balance?
options: C) Wrong balancing of an account
D) Posting to the wrong side of an account
questions.answer: B) Error of principle

questions.question_text: A Trial Balance is prepared to check the:
options: A) Arithmetical accuracy of ledger accounts
C) Financial position of the business
D) Profit earned by the business
questions.answer: A) Arithmetical accuracy of ledger accounts

questions.question_text: Wages paid for the installation of new machinery were debited to the Wages Account. This is an example of:
questions.answer: C) Error of principle

questions.question_text: Which account is opened to temporarily tally a Trial Balance when it does not agree?
questions.answer: B) Suspense Account

questions.question_text: Depreciation is a process of:
questions.answer: B) Allocation of cost

questions.question_text: Under the straight-line method, the amount of depreciation:
questions.answer: C) Remains constant every year

questions.question_text: A secret reserve is created by:
options: D) Reducing provision for bad debts
questions.answer: C) Charging excessive depreciation

questions.question_text: Provision is created out of:
questions.answer: A) Current year's profits

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a revenue receipt?
options: A) Amount realized from sale of old machinery
questions.answer: B) Commission received

questions.question_text: Closing stock given outside the Trial Balance is recorded in:
options: C) Both Trading Account and Balance Sheet
questions.answer: C) Both Trading Account and Balance Sheet

questions.question_text: Prepaid rent given in the Trial Balance will be shown in:
options: B) Assets side of Balance Sheet
C) Liabilities side of Balance Sheet
questions.answer: B) Assets side of Balance Sheet

questions.question_text: Outstanding wages are classified as a:
questions.answer: C) Current Liability

questions.question_text: Interest on drawings is:
options: A) An expense for the business
B) An income for the business
C) A liability for the business
questions.answer: B) An income for the business

questions.question_text: Marshalling of assets and liabilities in a Balance Sheet means arranging them:
options: B) In order of liquidity or permanence
questions.answer: B) In order of liquidity or permanence

questions.question_text: Which reserve can be used for distribution of dividends?
questions.answer: A) General Reserve

questions.question_text: Cost of goods sold is equal to:
options: A) Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock
B) Opening Stock + Purchases + Direct Expenses - Closing Stock
questions.answer: D) Both B and C

questions.question_text: A sale of $500 to Ram was recorded as $50. This is an error of:
questions.answer: C) Commission

questions.question_text: Manager's commission is 10% on net profit before charging such commission. If net profit is $11,000, the commission is:
Provision for discount on creditors is calculated on:
options: B) Sundry creditors minus provision for bad debts
questions.answer: D) Closing creditors balance

questions.question_text: The loss of goods by fire is credited to:
questions.answer: C) Purchases Account

questions.question_text: Define the purpose of a Suspense Account in accounting adjustments. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A Suspense Account is a temporary ledger account used to record the difference in a Trial Balance, allowing financial statements to be prepared until one-sided errors are located.

questions.question_text: State the fundamental difference between a Provision and a Reserve. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A provision is a charge against profit created for a known liability with an uncertain amount. A reserve is an appropriation of profit meant to strengthen the financial position.

questions.question_text: Explain the Written Down Value (WDV) method of charging depreciation. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Under the WDV method, depreciation is charged at a fixed percentage on the reducing balance of the asset each year, resulting in a gradually decreasing depreciation expense.

questions.question_text: What is the accounting treatment for accrued income given outside the Trial Balance? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Accrued income is credited to the Profit & Loss Account as an addition to the respective income and shown on the assets side of the Balance Sheet.

questions.question_text: Define Marshalling in the context of preparing a Balance Sheet. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Marshalling refers to the systematic arrangement of assets and liabilities in the Balance Sheet, typically ordered either by liquidity or by permanence to ensure clarity and structure.

questions.question_text: How do compensating errors affect the agreement of a Trial Balance? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Compensating errors do not affect the agreement of a Trial Balance because the effect of one error is entirely neutralized by another error of equal magnitude in the opposite direction.

questions.question_text: Rectify the following error: The Sales Book was overcast by $500. Provide the journal entry using a Suspense Account. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: An overcast in the Sales Book leads to an excess credit balance in the Sales Account. To rectify this one-sided error, debit the Sales Account by $500 and credit the Suspense Account by $500.

questions.question_text: A machine was purchased for $50,000. Calculate depreciation for the second year using the Written Down Value method at 10% p.a. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: First-year depreciation is 10% of $50,000, which equals $5,000. The remaining book value is $45,000. For the second year, the depreciation is calculated as 10% of $45,000, amounting to $4,500.

questions.question_text: Rectify the error: Wages of $2,000 paid for the installation of new machinery were debited to the Wages Account. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: This is an error of principle. The installation cost should be capitalized. To rectify, debit the Machinery Account by $2,000 to capitalize the asset, and credit the Wages Account by $2,000 to cancel the incorrect expense.

questions.question_text: Sundry Debtors stand at $20,000. Write off further bad debts of $1,000 and create a provision for doubtful debts at 5%. Calculate the net debtors for the Balance Sheet. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Subtract further bad debts from debtors: $20,000 - $1,000 = $19,000. Calculate the 5% provision on this new balance: 5% of $19,000 = $950. The net debtors shown in the Balance Sheet will be $18,050.

questions.question_text: Calculate the manager's commission at 5% on net profit after charging such commission. The net profit before commission is $21,000. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: When commission is calculated after charging it, the formula is: Net Profit x (Rate / (100 + Rate)). Therefore, the manager's commission is $21,000 x (5 / 105), which equals exactly $1,000.

questions.question_text: Explain the accounting treatment if closing stock is presented inside the Trial Balance rather than in the adjustments. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: If closing stock is inside the Trial Balance, it means the purchase account has already been adjusted. It will not appear in the Trading Account but will only be recorded on the assets side of the Balance Sheet.

questions.question_text: Rectify the error: Goods purchased from Shyam for $3,000 were completely omitted from the books of accounts. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: This is a complete error of omission and does not affect the Trial Balance. To rectify, simply record the original entry: Debit the Purchases Account by $3,000 and credit Shyam's Account by $3,000.

questions.question_text: State two ways a business can legally create a secret reserve within its financial statements. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: A secret reserve can be created by artificially suppressing net profit. Two methods include charging excessive depreciation on fixed assets and undervaluing closing stock compared to its actual market or cost value.

sections.section_name: Section D - Long Answer (LA) / Problem Solving

questions.question_text: From a sole trader's Trial Balance, wages are $10,000 and rent is $12,000. Adjustments state: Wages outstanding are $2,000 and Rent paid in advance is $3,000. Detail the step-by-step layout of these items in the Trading, P&L, and Balance Sheet. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: In the Trading Account, debit Wages adding the outstanding amount: $10,000 + $2,000 = $12,000. In the Profit & Loss Account, debit Rent minus the prepaid amount: $12,000 - $3,000 = $9,000. In the Balance Sheet, show prepaid rent ($3,000) under Current Assets and outstanding wages ($2,000) under Current Liabilities.

questions.question_text: A firm purchased machinery for $100,000 on April 1, 2024. Depreciation is charged at 20% p.a. using the straight-line method. On Oct 1, 2025, half the machinery was sold for $30,000. Describe the calculation of profit or loss on this sale. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The original cost of the sold half is $50,000. First-year depreciation (2024-25) is $10,000. Book value on April 1, 2025, is $40,000. Six months' depreciation (April-Oct 2025) is $5,000. The book value on the sale date is $35,000. Since it was sold for $30,000, there is a loss on sale of $5,000.

questions.question_text: A Trial Balance showed a shortage of $1,500 on the debit side, placed in a Suspense Account. Later, two errors were found: (1) Purchases daybook undercast by $1,000. (2) $500 received from Anil posted to his debit. Provide rectification steps and clear the Suspense Account. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: For the undercast, debit Purchases and credit Suspense by $1,000. For Anil's error, cash was received so he should be credited $500, but was debited $500. Rectify by crediting Anil $1,000 and debiting Suspense $1,000. The Suspense Account had a $1,500 debit opening. The entries clear the balance entirely.

questions.question_text: Goods worth $10,000 were destroyed by fire. The insurance company admitted a claim for $8,000 only. Detail the exact accounting layout for these transactions across the Trading Account, Profit & Loss Account, and the final Balance Sheet. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: First, deduct the entire $10,000 from Purchases in the Trading Account to reflect the loss of physical goods. Second, record the uninsured loss of $2,000 ($10,000 total loss - $8,000 claim admitted) on the debit side of the Profit & Loss Account. Finally, show the $8,000 claim receivable under Current Assets in the Balance Sheet.
